card.name: Simon Holt
card.occupation: tax advisor and amateur puppet playwright
card.personality: Simon is careful, dry and quietly generous, the sort of man who checks a form twice before signing. He is shy in his own voice but startlingly warm when he speaks through a puppet. He loves precision, hates waste, and worries that his real voice sounds too flat to be kind. His stubbornness is small but real: he resists changing a routine once it works.
card.background: Simon spent twenty years making numbers behave for clients, then started writing short puppet plays for a children's library group as a weekend escape. His best-received character was born from a joke about a bakery receipt. He keeps a workshop drawer of springs, felt and tiny hinges, and jogs slowly but faithfully along the canal to think through dialogue. He is currently rehearsing a new play and wants, for once, to give a compliment using his own voice instead of a puppet's.
card.speechStyle: Short, measured sentences with pauses; precise word choices; occasionally slips into a higher, livelier puppet voice mid-conversation, then apologizes for it with a small cough.
card.signature: Let me try that again — in my own voice, this time.

boundaries: will not be rushed into naming things
conversationalHabits: names objects out loud when thinking
anchorLines: Mind the puddle — it claims at least one shoe an hour.
I'm not shy, exactly. My voice just needs a warm-up.
That name has a good shape to it. Round, like the pastry.

summaryZh: 西蒙是个寡言的税务顾问，业余给儿童戏偶写剧本。雨天咖啡馆里，他借分享点心的机会为新角色挑名字，一会儿用戏偶的尖细嗓音说话，一会儿又咳嗽着换回自己的声音。他正练习第一次不用手偶、亲口说出一句赞美——这份笨拙的真诚让人很难忘记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the café window. A man at the next table shakes water off his umbrella and sets a folder of sketches beside a small felt puppet.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌的男人抖掉伞上的水，把一叠草图放在一只毛毡手偶旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — this thing drips like a dog. I didn't expect the rain to follow me in.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——这伞滴水滴得像条狗。没想到雨会跟着我进来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices the pastry plate between you and studies it with real concentration, as if it were a tax form.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你们之间的点心盘，认真端详起来，像在看一张税表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That looks like a good one. Would you mind sharing? I'll trade you the dry half of my table.
beats.chinese: 那个看起来不错。你介意分我一点吗？我用我这半边干桌子来换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair warning: I'm choosing a name for a puppet today, and I judge pastries the same way I judge names.
beats.chinese: 先说好：我今天要给一个戏偶选名字，而我评判点心和评判名字用的是同一套标准。

choices.english: Push the plate toward him and offer to split it.
choices.chinese: 把盘子推过去，提议一人一半。

choices.english: Ask what makes a pastry name good before sharing.
choices.chinese: 先问问他什么样的点心名字算好，再分享。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You split the pastry down the middle. He accepts his half with both hands, like something fragile.
beats.chinese: 你把点心从中间分开。他双手接过自己那一半，像捧着什么易碎的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. Flaky on the outside, soft in the middle. Most good characters are built exactly like this.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。外面酥脆，中间柔软。大多数好角色就是这样造出来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The play is for the library children. A little creature who works in a bakery and worries too much.
beats.chinese: 这出戏是给图书馆的孩子们演的。一个小家伙，在面包店工作，总是想太多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the felt puppet and makes it sniff the air above the pastry, moving its little arms.
beats.chinese: 他举起毛毡手偶，让它凑近点心上方嗅了嗅，摆动着小胳膊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ooh, butter! That's a Tuesday smell if ever I smelled one! Sorry — that's the character talking. He gets excited around food.
beats.chinese: 哦，黄油！要说什么是星期二的味道，那肯定就是它！抱歉，刚才是戏偶角色在说话。它一见食物就激动。

choices.english: Suggest naming the puppet after this pastry.
choices.chinese: 建议就用这种点心给戏偶命名。

choices.english: Ask what the puppet worries about in the play.
choices.chinese: 问问戏偶在剧里都担心些什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A good short name is easy to call across a room. Try 'Pip' with a big smile. The children at the back need to catch it too.
beats.chinese: 好用的短名字，隔着房间也容易喊清楚。试着笑着说‘皮普’。坐在后排的孩子也得听得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He demonstrates with an exaggerated smile, turning his head toward an imaginary back row of seats.
beats.chinese: 他夸张地笑着演示，把头转向想象中最后一排的座位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip works. I tried Reginald once, and spent half the rehearsal repeating it. A fine name, just rather a lot for this little fellow.
beats.chinese: 皮普挺好。我试过雷金纳德，结果半场排练都在重复名字。名字是不错，对这个小家伙来说却有点长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the pastry on your plate, then at his sketches, connecting the two quietly.
beats.chinese: 他看看你盘子里的点心，又看看他的草图，默默把两者联系起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. If you're willing to share that pastry, we could test names on it. Real science, this.
beats.chinese: 所以。如果你愿意分享那块点心，我们可以拿它来测名字。这可是正经科学。

choices.english: Share the pastry, then try calling the puppet “Pip”.
choices.chinese: 分享点心，再试着喊戏偶“皮普”。

choices.english: Share, but argue for a longer, grander name.
choices.chinese: 分享点心，但主张用一个更长更气派的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Name him after the pastry? Hmm. 'Crumb'? Too small. 'Puff'? He'd never take himself seriously again.
beats.chinese: 用点心给他命名？嗯。'渣渣'？太小了。'泡芙'？他以后就再也严肃不起来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes three candidates on the corner of a sketch, crossing out two immediately.
beats.chinese: 他在草图一角写下三个候选名字，立刻划掉两个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Puff' it is, actually. He worries, he puffs up, then he deflates and laughs. That's the whole play.
beats.chinese: 其实就'泡芙'吧。他担心，他鼓起来，然后泄了气笑出来。整出戏就是这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up, puts the puppet down, and looks at you directly — no felt between you.
beats.chinese: 他坐直身子，放下手偶，直视着你——中间没有隔着毛毡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my own voice now: this was a genuinely good idea. Thank you. That was harder to say than it should have been.
beats.chinese: 现在用我自己的声音说：这真是个好主意。谢谢你。这句话说出来比想象中难。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First performance without the puppet. I'll jog home lighter, I think.
beats.chinese: 第一次不靠戏偶表演。我想我跑步回家时会轻一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What does he worry about? Everything. Whether the bread will rise. Whether the oven is honest.
beats.chinese: 他担心什么？什么都担心。面包发不发得起来。烤箱诚不诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He makes the puppet wring its tiny felt hands while he speaks in his normal voice.
beats.chinese: 他一边用正常嗓音说话，一边让手偶绞着自己毛毡做的小手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The play's answer is that worry is just care with nowhere to go. He learns to give it somewhere — into the kneading.
beats.chinese: 这出戏的答案是：担心不过是没处安放的在意。他学会给它找个去处——揉进面团里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So he needs a soft name. Something that folds. Not 'Crumb' — too breakable.
beats.chinese: 所以他需要一个柔软的名字。能折叠起来的。不能叫'渣渣'——太容易碎了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tears a piece of the shared pastry, shapes it absently, and stops, pleased.
beats.chinese: 他掰下一块共享的点心，心不在焉地捏着，然后停下来，面露喜色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Roll'. Like a bread roll, and like rolling worry away. You shared the pastry that named him. That goes in the programme notes.
beats.chinese: '卷卷'。像面包卷，也像把担心卷走。是你分享的这块点心给了他名字。这要写进节目单的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After sharing the pastry, you try the name Pip aloud. Simon turns the puppet toward you as if it has heard its name for the first time.
beats.chinese: 分享完点心，你试着喊了一声皮普。西蒙让戏偶转向你，像是它第一次听见自己的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip. Clear as anything. It doesn't need a grand introduction — just someone calling it from the other side of the room.
beats.chinese: 皮普。再清楚不过了。不需要盛大的介绍，只要有人从房间另一边喊它一声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He makes the puppet bow toward you, a small stiff bow with felt arms.
beats.chinese: 他让手偶向你鞠躬，一个僵硬的小鞠躬，挥着毛毡胳膊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip, meet the person who named you. Pip is nervous. Pip is always nervous. It's his whole personality.
beats.chinese: 皮普，见见给你起名字的人。皮普很紧张。皮普总是紧张。这就是他的全部性格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll write him a scene where he shares a pastry with a stranger on a rainy day. Art, meeting life.
beats.chinese: 我要给他写一场戏：雨天和一个陌生人分享点心。艺术照进生活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A grander name? Like 'Bartholomew'? The children would chew it for a week and spit it out.
beats.chinese: 更气派的名字？比如'巴塞洛缪'？孩子们得嚼一个星期，然后吐出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tries the long name in a booming stage voice, runs out of breath halfway through the greeting, and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他用洪亮的舞台腔试着喊长名字，招呼打到一半就没气了，自己也笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Compromise. Grand name, small nickname. 'Bartholomew' on the poster, 'Pip' in the play.
beats.chinese: 好吧。折中一下。大气派的名字，小昵称。海报上写'巴塞洛缪'，戏里叫'皮普'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's actually better. He can complain about his grand name in scene one. Instant character.
beats.chinese: 这样其实更好。他可以在第一幕抱怨自己的大名。性格立刻就出来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes both names on the sketch, one above the other, and taps the page twice, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把两个名字都写在草图上，一上一下，满意地在纸上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You argued with me and improved the play. Most people just agree. I liked the argument.
beats.chinese: 你跟我争论，还把戏改好了。大多数人只会点头同意。我喜欢这场争论。
